title: The stone didn’t move so Jesus could get out.
paragraphs:
The stone didn’t move so Jesus could get out.
It moved so you could see He already did.

Before sunrise…
before sermons…
before the Church ever preached—
heaven broke the silence.

Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came carrying grief, not expectation.
Spices in hand. Hearts shattered. Dreams buried.
Because as far as they knew…
Jesus was still dead.

The cross had spoken.
Blood had been spilled.
The sky had gone dark.

And when Friday ends like that—
Sunday usually doesn’t come with hope.
But Scripture says:
“After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb.” — Matthew 28:1
They came to a grave.
But they stepped into glory.
“There was a violent earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven and, going to the tomb, rolled back the stone and sat on it.” — Matthew 28:2

Not frantic.
Not rushed.
Sat on it.
Like death had just been turned into a footstool.
The guards—trained killers—shook like children.
“The guards were so afraid of him that they shook and became like dead men.” — Matthew 28:4
But the women?
They were invited closer.
Because heaven doesn’t terrify those who are seeking Jesus.
It reveals.
“Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.” — Matthew 28:5
Catch that.

Not “who was mistaken.”
Not “who fainted.”
Who was crucified.

The Gospel never hides the brutality of sin.
It doesn’t soften the cross.
Jesus really died.

Your sin wasn’t theoretical.
It was nailed.
It bled.
It cost heaven everything.
But then—
the sentence that split history:
“He is not here; He has risen, just as He said.” — Matthew 28:6
Just. As. He. Said.

Not a backup plan.
Not divine improvisation.
Promise fulfilled.
Jesus had already declared it:
“The Son of Man must be delivered… be crucified and on the third day be raised again.” — Luke 24:7
And He did exactly that.
But here’s what we miss…
The resurrection is not just proof that Jesus is powerful.
It’s proof that His sacrifice was accepted.
“He was delivered over to death for our sins and was raised to life for our justification.” — Romans 4:25

That means the debt is paid.
The wrath is satisfied.
The door is open.

Sin said, “You’re guilty.”
The cross said, “It is finished.” — John 19:30
The empty tomb said, “You’re free.”
Let this hit you deep—

The same power that rolled that stone…
is the same power that can roll addiction off your life.

The same voice that walked out of the grave…
can call you out of depression, shame, and hidden sin.
“I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die.” — John 11:25
This is not religion.
This is rescue.
Some of you are still living like the tomb is full.

Still bound.
Still hiding.
Still believing lies that were buried 2,000 years ago.
But hear me—

Jesus is not in that grave.
And you don’t have to be either.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!” — 2 Corinthians 5:17

You don’t clean yourself up to come to Him.
You come to Him—and He raises you.

From guilt.
From bondage.
From death itself.
And here’s the invitation:

Repent.
Turn.
Believe.

Not in a concept.
Not in a system.
In a risen Savior.
“If you declare with your mouth, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.” — Romans 10:9

Saved.
Not improved.
Resurrected.
If this stirred something in you… don’t ignore it.
That’s not emotion.
That’s God calling you out of the tomb.

Because the stone is still rolled away.
The tomb is still empty.
And Jesus is still alive.
